4m^{2} – 7mn + 3n^{2} + m – n =
A. (m – n)(4m – 3n + 1).
B. (m – n)(4m + 3n + 1).
C. (m + n)(4m – 3n – 1).
D. (m + n)(4m + 3n – 1).
Solution
Key Steps: • Group the terms.
• Use the cross-method.
•  Take out the common factor.
4m^{2} – 7mn + 3n^{2} + m – n
= (4m^{2} – 7mn + 3n^{2}) + (m – n)  → •
= (4m – 3n)(m – n) + (m – n)  → •
= (m – n)(4m – 3n + 1)  → →
∴ The answer is A.

h^{2} – 3h – 4k^{2} – 6k =
A. (h – 2k)(h – 2k + 3).
B. (h – 2k)(h + 2k + 3).
C. (h + 2k)(h – 2k – 3).
D. (h + 2k)(h + 2k – 3).
Solution
Key Steps: • Group the terms.
• Use a^{2} – b^{2} ≡ (a + b)(a – b).
•  Take out the common factor.
h^{2} – 3h – 4k^{2} – 6k
= (h^{2} – 4k^{2}) – (3h + 6k)  → •
= (h + 2k)(h – 2k) – 3(h + 2k)  → • and →
= (h + 2k)(h – 2k – 3)  → →
∴ The answer is C.
